title: Template dashboards v1: RAG + Agents + recommended alert rules (naming + publish steps)
author: Sergio Costa
release_notes:
- Adds prebuilt dashboards for Quickstart Templates (RAG + Agents): latency breakdown, retrieval quality signals, tool loop health, token economics.
- Adds recommended alert rules + SLO examples with conservative defaults (opt-in).
- Documents metric naming + tag cardinality guidance and publish/versioning steps.
description: Context: DevEx Quickstart Templates (RAG + agents) are standardizing OTel instrumentation and a small set of Redwood-specific metrics/attributes. This PR ships the initial dashboard + alerts pack in `observability-pack` so template apps have a first-run observability experience and internal Support/SRE can quickly triage common failures (401/429/timeouts/tool errors/retrieval empty). Scope: (1) dashboards (Grafana JSON) and (2) alert rules (Prometheus-style) + (3) documentation for metric naming conventions, required labels, and publish steps for release tagging. Dashboards included: (a) `Templates / RAG + Agents Overview` (golden signals + error taxonomy rollup) (b) `Templates / RAG Latency Breakdown` (gateway + model + retrieval + tool time; p50/p95; streaming disconnect rate) (c) `Templates / Retrieval Health` (retrieval hit rate, empty result rate, top-k distribution, chunking defaults sanity) (d) `Templates / Agent Tools` (tool call rate, tool error rate by tool_name, tool output truncation, max-iterations hits) (e) `Templates / Token Economics` (input/output tokens, cache hit %, effective $/1k tokens proxy, saturation signals). Alerts included (opt-in, documented as recommendations not defaults): (1) High 5xx rate for template-tagged traffic (2) Elevated 429 rate (rate limit pressure) (3) Streaming disconnects above threshold (4) Tool failure rate sustained (5) Retrieval empty results sustained (guard against misconfigured index/env). Naming conventions / cardinality: aligns with `observability-hooks-standard` and `quickstart-tracing-conventions`: metric namespace `redwood.template.*` (NOT `redwood.quickstart.*`), required low-cardinality labels only: `service.name`, `deployment.environment`, `template.name`, `template.version`, `model`, `region` (where available), `http.status_code` (bucketed), and `error.type` from the template taxonomy. `tool.name` is allowed but must be explicitly enumerated in the template (no user-provided arbitrary tool names), and dashboards/alerts include a note to disable tool_name breakdown if a customer adds dynamic tools. Publish steps: adds `docs/publishing.md` describing version bump, changelog entry, dashboard schema validation, and how DevEx references the pack from template READMEs. Notes: This PR intentionally avoids adoption telemetry (template header/tagging) since that lives in gateway + console filtering; dashboards include an optional variable `template_tag` to filter traffic when the tag is present, but they do not require it to function.

conversation: Allison Grant (review): The dashboards look good, but we need to lock the metric namespace and labels before this ships. Please align to `redwood.template.*` and ensure we do not encourage high-cardinality labels. Specifically: remove any panel that groups by `request_id`/`trace_id`, avoid `user_id`, and confirm `tool_name` is safe (enumerated). Also, can you add a short section documenting which labels are required vs optional? Sergio Costa (author): Updated metric namespace across all queries to `redwood.template.*`. Removed the one panel that grouped by `http.target` (it was too spiky); replaced with route templates and status code buckets. Added `docs/metrics_naming_conventions.md` with required/optional labels and a callout that request_id/trace_id are logs/traces only. For `tool.name`, added a note in the dashboard and docs: only safe if tools are statically defined; otherwise disable the breakdown variable. Christine Wong (SRE review): Alert thresholds feel aggressive for a template. We don’t want noisy defaults. Can we clearly mark these as recommended/opt-in and set conservative windows (10–15m) with burn-rate examples instead of tight p95 thresholds? Also please include a runbook link placeholder. Sergio Costa (author): Adjusted alerts to be opt-in; widened windows to 15m, added burn-rate style examples and `runbook_url` placeholders, and updated `alerts/README.md` to stress ‘copy/adapt’ guidance. Logan Wright (telemetry/analytics): In the Overview dashboard, the filter variable `template_tag` is good. Please ensure dashboards work without it; some proxies strip unknown headers and not all users will have the tag. Sergio Costa (author): Confirmed dashboards key off emitted metrics/traces only; tag filter is optional. Added a note that template tagging is optional and might be disabled in some environments. Caleb Johnson (ingestion): Please make sure queries use stable OTel semantic conventions where possible (`service.name`, `deployment.environment`). If using custom attributes, prefix with `redwood.*`. Sergio Costa (author): Updated label names accordingly. Any custom label in examples is now `redwood.template.name` / `redwood.template.version` and documented. Monica Patel (DevEx): Can we add a short ‘Verification’ section: what a user should see locally when running docker-compose collector + template? Helps support deflection. Sergio Costa (author): Added ‘Verification’ section to `README.md` with expected panels and a minimal checklist. Allison Grant (final): Approved after naming/cardinality and opt-in alerting changes. Please make sure we cut a release tag and update the DevEx docs PR to point at the versioned artifact. Sergio Costa: Will do—added publish steps doc and will cut `observability-pack@v0.9.0` after merge.
merge_outcome: Merged to main; release tag to be cut after merge per docs/publishing.md
